texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Saroj Kumar Mukhiya, aged about 19 years, suffered injuries. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 05.09.2020 at about 11:00 p.m., victim Saroj Kumar Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs Rajesh Kumar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90183634/ 1 Mukhiya alongwith his collegue Naveen Kumar Ray was returning from duty to their house on a bicycle. Victim Naveen Kumar Ray was riding the bicycle and Saroj Kumar Mukhiya was sitting behind him. When they reached near old ADC Office, Sec-15 A, Faridabad, Haryana, a Hundai Creta car bearing no. HR 29AM 5550 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came driven in a reckless manner, at a high speed and the bicycle. Due to the impact, both the riders on the bicycle fell and sustained injuries. While victim Naveen Kumar Ray died in the accident, victim Saroj sustained injuries. Victims were taken to Metro Hospital Sec-16 A Faridabad where victim Naveen Kumar was declared brought death and treatment was provided to victim Saroj. 3. An FIR No.0337/2020 dated 06.09.2020 u/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Faridabad Central, Haryana. Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle before concerned criminal court while the present claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by MACT NO:84/21 Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs. Rajesh Kumar & ors. P.No. 2 Of 18 ss respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. 5. No reply was filed by respondent no.1 despite opportunity. Respondent no. 2 filed a reply denying liability. It has been pleaded that respondent no. 1 had a valid DL and the offending vehicle was duly insured at the time of accident. In its reply, Respondent no.3 denied liability on the ground that the FIR was initially registered against an unknown vehicle and that the claim is collusive. It is however, admitted that the offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident. 6. From the pleadings, following issues were framed on 26.07.2020. OPP. 4) Relief. 7. In order to prove his claim, petitioner examined himself as PW-1. He examined himself by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the petition and stated that on 05.09.2020, at about 11:00 PM, he alongwith his colleague Naveen Kumar Ray were going to their rented house after finishing his job/work on a bicycle. Naveen Kumar was plying bicycle and PW1 was sitting Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs Rajesh Kumar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90183634/ 2 behind him. The bicycle was being plied on the correct side of the road. When they reached near old ADC Office, Sec-15 A Faridabad, Haryana, a Hundai Creta Car MACT NO:84/21 Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs. Rajesh Kumar & ors. P.No. 3 Of 18 ss bearing no. HR 29 AM 5550 came from Sun Flag Chowk at a high speed, driven in rash and negligent manner and hit the bicycle. Due to the forceful impact PW1 sustained grievous injuries, head injury and fracture while his friend Naveen sustained fatal injury. The passerby gathered and took him to metro hospital sec-16 A Faridabad. His MLC No. 5857/2020 was prepared. He was discharged but his treatment as outdoor patient continues till date. He deposed that he was unable to work after the accident. He deposed that an FIR bearing no. 0337/2020 was registered. He deposed that he was working a Tea Shop (Soya Chaap Express) Khokha no. 14, Sec-15 Faridabad Market, and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month. PW1, relied upon his MLC Ex.PW1/1, his discharge summery as Ex.PW1/2, OPD card and medical bills as Ex.PW1/3 and his ID proof (Aadhar Card and Pan Card) as Ex.PW1/4. He also relied upon charge-sheet as Ex.PW1/5. He was duly cross examined by counsel for insurance company. 8. Respondents did not lead any evidence despite opportunity. Final arguments in detail were addressed on behalf the Petitioner as well as the insurance company.
texts.arguments: In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of MACT NO:84/21 Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs. Rajesh Kumar & ors. P.No. 5 Of 18 ss charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 15. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court relies MACT NO:84/21 Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs. Rajesh Kumar & ors. P.No. 6 Of 18 ss upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T.Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Contro (India) (P) Ltd. And Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors . (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 . The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 16. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs Rajesh Kumar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90183634/ 4 Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured MACT NO:84/21 Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs. Rajesh Kumar & ors. P.No. 7 Of 18 ss would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). MACT NO:84/21 Saroj Kumar Mukhiya vs. Rajesh Kumar & ors. P.No. 8 Of 18 ss 16.5.
